clue.text: Use for special clothing

definitions.meaning: use in the sense of custom or regular practice, a settled way of behaving
the distinctive robe worn by a monk or nun, or a rider's outfit

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a routine or custom; the other is a garment such as a nun's or a riding outfit.

clue.text: Hold on-some men read her escapist stories!

indicators.note: some of the letters of these words, read straight through, give the answer

explanation.surface: Readers keep clinging to the escapist yarns some men enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals that the answer sits inside 'read her escapist', across the word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick fast or cling to something is to hold on to it.

clue.text: A combination that makes a nice change after all

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters are placed after the word all

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of a nice

explanation.surface: Someone praises a pairing that makes a pleasant difference after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns A NICE into IANCE, and 'after' puts it behind ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A union or pact between parties is a combination of them for a shared purpose.

clue.text: Disastrous commercial lines

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
lines of poetry make verse

explanation.surface: A dreadful advertising jingle.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful or unfavourable, as in adverse effects that bring misfortune.

clue.text: Causing no harm at a scene of great conflict

indicators.note: causing suggests the letters of no harm at are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing no damage at the site of a famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Causing' is an odd anagram signal: the letters of NO HARM AT are worked into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks defeated the Persians at this plain in 490 BC, a famous battlefield.

clue.text: Learns discipline and drive

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
to train is to discipline or drill

explanation.surface: A student learns self-discipline and motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: CON meaning to study is an old verb that crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or force someone is to drive them to act.

clue.text: Comes down on idle characters making a bad slip

indicators.note: on means the first piece goes on, ahead of, the second in this down-reading charade order

parts.note: comes down to earth, as a plane lands

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, of idle are rearranged to form the ending

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles down on a lazy group and takes a nasty fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' signals that the letters of IDLE are rearranged into LIDE; 'on' puts LANDS before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of earth and rock sliding down a hillside is a disastrous slip.

clue.text: There's many a cheat in Burgundy

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
taken as written
a con is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: Plenty of swindlers operate in the French wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: M for 'many' comes from the Roman numeral for 1000.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine from this town in southern Burgundy is a type of burgundy.

clue.text: Honour a quiet fellow

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone pays tribute to a reserved man.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a man or bloke, a synonym for fellow.

clue.text: Admire the sapient also

parts.note: to admire something is to like it
sapient means wise

explanation.surface: An instruction to look up to the learned, too.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning in the same way or too, a synonym for also.

clue.text: Rough though sound beast

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for the beast is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a horse is a beast

explanation.surface: A creature that is coarse yet healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'healthy', describing the beast, but it signals a word heard aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasping, harsh voice is rough.

clue.text: Flighty creature writing a note to servicemen

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fickle being pens a message to soldiers and sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' looks like 'fickle' but means able to fly; RN is Britain's Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird is a creature of flight.

clue.text: Perhaps one requires a different setting for a gemstone

indicators.note: a different setting means the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A jeweller suggests one stone might need remounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires a different setting' sounds like jewellery talk but tells us to rearrange PERHAPS plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious blue stone, one of the classic gems.

clue.text: Seen being cut by mellow old monarch, coloured

indicators.note: being cut by means the word seen is split open to take the other letters

parts.note: to age is to mellow, as wine or cheese does
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A sighting interrupted by a gentle elderly king in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut by' puts AGE and GR inside SEEN; GR is George Rex, an old British king's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyish-green shade named after the herb, so a colour description.

clue.text: Church getting in supply for a baseball player

indicators.note: getting in means church goes inside the word for supply

parts.note: to cater is to supply food

explanation.surface: A church brings in a provider for a ballplayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' puts CH inside CATER.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder behind home plate who receives the pitches.

clue.text: A small bed designed for road and rail transport and the small home

parts.note: a car is road transport
RY is short for railway
a cot is a small cottage

explanation.surface: A compact bed built for travel by road and rail and at home.
explanation.walkthrough: COT here is a little cottage, not a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable bed for a baby, carried by handles.

clue.text: Distraught when it's turned over in foreign currency

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside the currency

parts.note: the franc was France's currency

indicators.note: turned over means the letters of it are read backwards

parts.note: the word it

explanation.surface: Someone is upset when their money flips over abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes TI from IT, and 'in' places it inside FRANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild with worry, frenzied, so deeply distraught.

clue.text: Repaired-put in order again

definitions.meaning: repaired as in went to or had recourse to, as one repairs to a bar

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is went or turned to; the other, split as re-sorted, is ordered anew.

clue.text: A flash and trendy worker set about a high-minded individual

indicators.note: set about means the first pieces are placed around the other

parts.note: in means fashionable
an ant is a worker insect
ST is a saint

explanation.surface: A fashionable labourer surrounds a virtuous person in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' wraps IN and ANT around ST, the abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment, a split second, like a flash.

clue.text: Capital investment for a speculator's family

parts.note: a bear is a speculator who sells expecting a fall
kin means family

explanation.surface: Putting money into a stock trader's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital investment' means something you put on your head (the guards' tall fur hat), not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall fur hat of the Guards is something placed on the head, the caput.

clue.text: Bamboozles the young

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is fools or teases; the other is children.

clue.text: A quarter refuse such a decoration

parts.note: S, south, is a quarter of the compass
ash is waste from a fire, refuse

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a district's ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of cloth worn across the body as an honour or decoration.

clue.text: Stayed to reorganise firm

indicators.note: to reorganise means the letters of stayed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company stayed on to restructure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable and unwavering, as in a firm hand.

clue.text: The writer is on fire!

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Scottish poet; the other means blazes.

clue.text: Extremely worn

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Extremely worn' (6): that defines FRAYED, not the printed answer PRAYED; no wordplay gives PRAYED, so the clue or answer is garbled.

clue.text: Put under treatment-so disturbed

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of put under are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient is anaesthetised for surgery and so feels upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put under' looks medical but is the anagram fodder; 'treatment' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil turned up by a spade has been dug over and disturbed.

clue.text: Drank hard back in the military station

indicators.note: back means the word for drank hard is read backwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Someone drank heavily back at the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOPED round.
explanation.definitionFit: A base where military stores are kept or troops assemble.

clue.text: Finding rare Continental articles, spent

parts.note: un is a French article
der is a German article
done means finished, spent

explanation.surface: Discovering unusual European items, all used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' looks like 'unusual' but is how a steak is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked lightly so it is still red inside is rare.
